summary.name: QEMU
summary.one_liner: QEMU is a generic, open source machine emulator and virtualizer that can run whole operating systems or Linux/BSD user-mode programs on different CPU architectures.
keywords: run operating systems in a vm
use_cases: run operating systems for other machine architectures
run Linux or BSD programs built for another CPU
run KVM or Xen virtual machines
test software on different hardware architectures
virtualize systems with near native performance
summary.what_it_does: QEMU is a generic, open source machine emulator and virtualizer. In full-system mode it runs operating systems for any supported machine architecture. In user-mode it runs programs built for another Linux or BSD target on a different architecture. It can also be used with KVM and Xen to run virtual machines with near native performance. The page lists current release branches (for example 11.1.3 and 11.0.5) and a link to the full release list.
notable: Full-system emulation for any supported architecture
KVM and Xen acceleration with near-native performance
caveats: The page does not name macOS or Windows as host platforms, though the awesome-mac listing places it under macOS resources.
Near-native performance is stated for KVM and Xen use; other modes are not described for speed.
